ety.text: From up- + date. Earliest usages from 1940s (see Citations).

senses.d: An additional piece of information, an addition to existing information.
ex: I just made an update to my blog about my trip to Rome.

senses.d: An advisement providing more up-to-date information than currently known.
ex: He gave me an update on the situation in New York.

senses.d: A modification of something to a more recent, up-to-date version; (in software) a minor upgrade.
ex: Our database receives an update every morning at 3 AM.
I have a couple of updates to install on your laptop.

senses.d: An adjustment of parameters in a model, or the rule by which they are adjusted.
A version of something which is newer than other versions.
ex: You should try the update: it rocks.
The mid-season update for MW3 is here, introducing quite a bit of content across all three of CoD’s modes.

senses.d: To bring (a thing) up to date.
ex: I need to update my records to take account of the most recent transaction.

senses.d: To bring (a person) up to date: to inform (a person) about recent developments.
ex: Update me on what happened while I was away.

senses.d: To change one's credence in a proposition in response to new evidence.
ex: I need to update on the new data.
How can I update my priors?
